title: Lifting a projective-bundle fibre isomorphism as a morphism
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], E a quasi-coherent finite locally free module of constant rank r >= 2 [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and p:P(E)->S the canonical symmetric-algebra relative Proj [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]. Let M,N be invertible modules on P(E) [def-sc-invertible-module], and s a point of S. Assume the tensor-formula pullbacks of M,N to the residue-field fibre at s are isomorphic [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-module-pullback]. There exist an open U containing s and a morphism phi:M|p^{-1}(U)->N|p^{-1}(U) such that its tensor-formula pullback along the fibre inclusion of p|U at the point (s,s in U) is an isomorphism. No invertibility of phi over p^{-1}(U) itself is asserted.

proof.text: A finite locally free module is finite type, so the identity closed immersion presents the canonical bundle projection as projective in the projective-bundle sense. Apply projectiveBundle_proper.

proof.text: Apply projective_bundle_fiber_geometry: the projection is flat and locally of finite presentation, its fibres are geometrically reduced and connected, and H1(O) of each fibre vanishes. ProperFlatGlobalSections supplies the universal structure-pushforward unit isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put L=M dual tensor N. It is invertible. Pullback of dual evaluation gives a tensor inverse pairing for the pulled-back M and its dual. Combine that pairing with the assumed fibre isomorphism and the tensor-pullback comparison to trivialize L on the fibre.

proof.text: Apply picard_h1_local_section_of_base_descent_generator with n=0, W=S, k=id. All test-family hypotheses are vacuous; H1(O)=0 makes the map to the empty product injective. The fibre line descends from the unit over Spec kappa(s). Obtain a section of L on a base-open pullback generating at every point of the marked fibre.

proof.text: On this proper base change let D be the generating locus. The complement of the closed image of Y minus D is an open W through the marked point. For every test map with image in W its induced map q to Y lands in D. The free generator on D pulls back to a global free generator. homOfGlobalSection is an isomorphism, so tensor-pullback composition trivializes L on the smaller base-open pullback. The helper trivial_near_fiber_generator proves this argument while retaining the actual unit rather than an unspecified finite locally free module.

source.place: lemma-H1-O-multiple-picard-flat-proper (Tag 0BF2), empty comparison family; proper shrinking on the generating locus and tensor cancellation (Modules, Tag 01CY).

proof.text: Take the image U of W in the original base open. Compare the pullback scheme with the preimage open subscheme. Tensor the trivialization of L with the restricted M and compose the pulled-back dual evaluation M tensor (M dual tensor N) isomorphic to N. This gives an actual isomorphism between the two restricted lines. Use its hom as phi; every functor preserves isomorphisms, so its tensor pullback to the restricted fibre is invertible.

lean.statement:
theorem projective_bundle_fiber_hom_lift (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules)
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (M N : (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProj.Modules)
    (hM : M.IsInvertible) (hN : N.IsInvertible) (s : S)
    (e : Nonempty
      ((tensorPullback
        ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom.fiberι s)).obj M ≅
        (tensorPullback
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom.fiberι s)).obj N)) :
    ∃ (U : S.Opens) (hs : s ∈ U)
      (φ : (tensorPullback
        ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).obj M ⟶
        (tensorPullback
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).obj N),
      IsIso ((tensorPullback
        (((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ∣_ U).fiberι
          (⟨s, hs⟩ : U.toScheme))).map φ)
